subject: Clinical AI data pipeline at [COMPANY] with [NAME]
text:
Hi [NAME],  

 I saw [COMPANY] standardized 88% of prior-auth volume and now processes 83% in real time. Big milestone, congrats! 

 We're working with a top-three US payer and Highmark Health to help them with the clinician review-and-audit layer underneath that kind of automation. 

 I'd love your thoughts on how we've helped them scale the review without losing the audit trail. Happy to share what's been working and what hasn't. 

 I'm free this Wednesday afternoon.

subject: Vision at Mount Sinai
text:
Hi [NAME],  

 We work with Iterative Scopes and Proximie on the data layer for clinical video AI.  

 The Mount Sinai partnership caught my attention. Eight hospitals and 100,000 procedures is a significant production milestone. 

 Teams moving into computer vision whilst scaling clinical AI come to us when: 

 - Each new hospital site introduces OR environments the model hasn't seen. 

 - Precision degradation at a flagship customer is a commercial risk before it's a technical one 

 - The data infrastructure that proved the product in a pilot wasn't built to support the retraining cadence a new production deployment requires 

 Do you face similar issues at [COMPANY]? 

 If so, it might be worth having an initial conversation to see whether our offerings fit your needs. I'm free this Thursday if that works.

subject: pittsburgh. what changed.
text:
Hi [NAME],  

 Quick one. my team works with Flock Safety on annotation and model evaluation for their LPR detection catalogue across hundreds of municipalities.

subject: Less time finding data, more time on models
text:
Hi [NAME], 

I saw the company's hiring pages for engineering roles and noticed your deep learning for fruit defect detection models. 

We work with companies like John Deere on a similar detection workflow. Encord is the curation and annotation infrastructure that sits underneath their image-based defect and quality detection models. 

When their model got a new defect class wrong, they found the right training examples faster because Encord surfaced them automatically instead of engineers hunting through images manually.

With iQS Pro expanding into new geographies and fruit varieties, I thought i'd reach out before the annotation pipeline becomes a bottleneck. 

Do you have 20 minutes next week to compare notes on how you're managing that today?

subject: when eo/ir data meets rf
text:
Hi [NAME],  

 I saw the MoU with Ecliptic Defence and Space, combining electro-optical/infrared and RF sensor data for situational awareness. 

 we work with Forterra on the labelling and QA behind edge-deployed defence perception models. Combining two sensor types usually means combining two labelling standards too, before either model can trust the other's ground truth. 

 pulling two teams worth of training data into one pipeline is the kind of thing that slows your entire engineering team down.  

 I'm curious how that's being scoped? 

 Do you have some time to connect early next week? If so, let me know and ill send over a link.

subject: FDA June Update - every model update needs its own trail
text:
Hi [NAME],

The FDA's June 17 classification for DICOM ML-based radiology devices makes
annotation documentation a legal special control. Combined with CE marking,
eyonis LCS now operates under two parallel post-market documentation
regimes.

The risk: when a regulatory reviewer asks for subgroup-level annotation
evidence behind the last model update, where does that trail live?

We work with Conavi Medical on exactly this: annotation provenance and
audit trail for a regulated imaging AI device.

Is this something you have a process for? Happy to connect this week if
useful.

subject: Data flywheel for L4 autonomy
text:
Hi [NAME] - been following Kakaomobility for some time, and after seeing the recent announcement at COEX around the L4 autonomy roadmap, I thought it would be a great time to get introduced. 

For context, I work on the Physical AI team at Encord, partnering with companies like Woven by Toyota to provide the platform and workforce that scale real-world data pipelines, supporting the journey from L2/L3 to L4 autonomy. We help teams gain greater control over data curation by surfacing the right scenes and edge cases, while enabling frontier use cases such as VLA reasoning and 3D auto-labeling. 

I think there's pieces that could match well with your roadmap. Would you be open to a quick chat later this week? Happy to share what we've learned from supporting other teams on a similar journey.

subject: Point rapide sur Spimed AI
text:
Bonjour [NAME],

[SENDER] de faire ta connaissance. Je travaille avec [SENDER] chez Encord.

Je relisais vos échanges précédents autour des projets de Spimed AI sur
l'analyse de plaque, la dissection aortique et l'embolie pulmonaire.

Je sais qu'à l'époque vous aviez choisi RedBrick, principalement parce que
cela faisait plus de sens commercialement pour la première phase. Je
voulais simplement savoir si les choses avaient évolué depuis, en
particulier sur la labellisation des plaques, les workflows de revue
radiologue ou les besoins de traçabilité FDA.

Nous avons aussi compris que RedBrick commençait à réduire ses opérations,
et nous avons récemment vu plusieurs équipes passer sur Encord en raison
d'une baisse de capacité d'ingénierie et de support de leur côté.

De ce que vous aviez discuté avec [SENDER], la plaque semblait être le sujet
où la qualité d'annotation, le consensus entre reviewers et l'auditabilité
pouvaient devenir plus importants à mesure que le projet avançait.

Je serai à Paris la semaine prochaine avec notre équipe MedTech. Ce serait
super de prendre un café ou un déjeuner si tu as un moment.
